breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer brokerages and banks in South Korea should treat the wave of attacks on financial firms as ongoing: the same pattern — abnormal external access to web-facing login and internal systems — has now hit a major brokerage days after the regulator disclosed 40 incidents at 37 firms. Firms should review web login and groupware access controls, watch for phishing and impersonation using the exposed employee contact details and customer account numbers, and check whether staff credentials need resetting given the encrypted passwords exposed.
breaking.headline: Mirae Asset Securities discloses breach of 3,800 customer account numbers and 35,255 employee records
breaking.known: The firm said abnormal external access was detected on 4 November against its mobile-web phone-authentication login service and on 5 November against its internal groupware system (mi-global); the access routes were blocked immediately and an emergency response was activated. About 3,800 customers' account numbers were exposed; the firm says no account-holder names or other sensitive customer information leaked with them. Personal data of 35,255 current employees, retirees and outsourced staff was also exposed, including names, employee numbers, email addresses, mobile phone numbers and encrypted passwords. Resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's licence numbers and other unique identifiers were not exposed. The firm's co-CEOs apologised in a public notice. The incident was reported to the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service and the Personal Information Protection Commission. The disclosure follows a wave of breaches across South Korean financial firms — the FSC said on 5 November that 40 incidents had been reported at 37 firms — and is a separate incident from the 28 October Mirae Asset Global Investments disclosure, which involved a different entity and no customer data.
breaking.source_name: AlphaBiz, 7 November 2026 (translated from Korean); Korea Times, 7 November 2026
breaking.summary: Mirae Asset Securities, one of South Korea's largest brokerages, said on 7 November 2026 that external attacks on 4–5 November exposed the account numbers of about 3,800 customers and personal data of 35,255 current and former employees and contractors, including names, employee numbers, email addresses, mobile phone numbers and encrypted passwords. The firm says no malware infection or service disruption occurred, no financial loss has been confirmed, and its main systems are operating normally. The incident was reported to the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service and the Personal Information Protection Commission.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: The attack method and the attacker's identity are undisclosed, and the firm has not said how the attackers reached the two systems. Whether the exposed account numbers or employee data have been misused has not been reported.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Malaysian banks and APAC peers should watch for a formal statement from Bank Rakyat and for any leaked data sample, and warn customers against phishing that cites the incident. The claim of internal access, if true, would make this a breach rather than a defacement; until the bank confirms or denies it, treat the internal-access claim as unconfirmed and the website defacement and outage as confirmed.
breaking.headline: Bank Rakyat website defaced by actor claiming internal access; bank confirms outage
breaking.known: Pages on the bank's official web portal, including informational pages on personal financing, were briefly defaced on the evening of 6 November; the defacement was first reported on social media and the pages were restored within about an hour. The defacement notice read: “Marlanwg is here. We have successfully accessed the internal infrastructure and retrieved a sample of your data to verify the extent of the breach”, and directed bank officials to the encrypted messaging app Session to negotiate data deletion and remediation terms. At 23:45 on 6 November the bank said its corporate website was unavailable and told customers to use its iRakyat, BRICK, QR2E and i-bizRAKYAT apps and platforms. Bank Negara Malaysia previously fined Bank Rakyat RM1 million under its Risk Management in Technology framework after a separate cybersecurity breach.
breaking.source_name: Pokde.Net, 6 November 2026; Siakap Keli, 6 November 2026 (translated from Malay)
breaking.summary: Malaysian cooperative bank Bank Rakyat's corporate website was briefly defaced on the evening of 6 November 2026 by an actor using the handle “Marlanwg”, who claimed to have accessed the bank's internal infrastructure and taken a sample of its data. The bank confirmed at 23:45 that its corporate website was unavailable and directed customers to its mobile apps and digital platforms. The defaced pages were restored within about an hour, but the bank has not confirmed or denied the actor's claim of internal access.
breaking.unknown: The bank has not issued a formal statement confirming or denying the claim of internal network access or data theft, and no data sample has been independently verified. Whether customer data or funds are affected, and whether the bank's wider digital services are fully restored, is unconfirmed.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer banks and consumer-finance firms that outsource loan guarantees should check whether their customers' data passed through the affected system, prepare for phishing and identity-fraud attempts using the leaked licence numbers and income data, and warn affected customers not to trust calls, emails or messages that cite their loan details. The leak of driver's licence numbers together with income and guarantee amounts is directly usable for impersonation and social engineering against bank customers.
breaking.headline: SMBC Consumer Finance discloses breach of up to 321,018 customers' data
breaking.known: SMBC Consumer Finance detected unauthorised access to its loan-guarantee system on 2 November and cut off access the same day; data was sent outside the company. The leaked data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, driver's licence numbers, employer and income details, and guarantee amounts and other contract information. Images of identity documents were not included. The firm provides guarantee services to 189 financial institutions, including regional banks, credit unions and online banks; its own Promise consumer-finance service does not use the affected system and is unaffected. No secondary harm from misuse of the data had been confirmed at the time of disclosure. Since the disclosure, partner banks have confirmed their customers are among those affected: Docomo SMTB Net Bank said up to 122,635 of its customers may be affected; Hiroshima Bank said personal data of customers who applied for two of its loan products was in the leak and suspended web applications for them; Chugoku Bank said up to 25 records were affected and also suspended web applications. (Nikkei, 6 November 2026.)
breaking.source_name: Nikkei, 5 November 2026; TBS NEWS DIG, 5 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
breaking.summary: SMBC Consumer Finance, the Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group consumer-finance arm, said on 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to its loan-guarantee system exposed personal data of up to 321,018 people, including names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, driver's licence numbers, employer details, income and loan guarantee amounts. The intrusion was detected on 2 November and access was cut off the same day; the guarantee system is suspended while checks continue. No misuse of the data has been confirmed so far, and images of identity documents were not included. The data covers customers of 189 partner banks, credit unions and online banks for which the firm provides loan guarantees; its own Promise consumer-finance service was not affected.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: The full list of affected partner institutions is still being pinned down — Hiroshima Bank, Chugoku Bank and Docomo SMTB Net Bank have confirmed their customers are affected, and Fukuoka Bank is still checking. Whether the intrusion exploited a specific vulnerability, and the attacker's identity, are undisclosed.

breaking.bfsi_impact: A leaked list of 227,216 corporate customer email addresses is ready-made fuel for targeted phishing and business-email compromise impersonating SMBC. Peer banks using third-party email-delivery services should check their own suppliers' exposure, and customers should treat any message citing SMBC business as suspect unless verified through known channels.
breaking.headline: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation confirms 227,216 email addresses leaked via contractor
breaking.known: The leak came through Arara's email-delivery service 'Arara Message', used by the bank. The affected addresses are recipients of bank emails sent 1 July–31 October 2026, mainly corporate customers plus some sole proprietors. No account numbers, balances, PINs or internet-banking IDs or passwords were included. The bank was told of the unauthorised access on 28 October and received confirmation that data had leaked on 2 November. SMBC and SMBC Trust Bank also announced a new information-sharing arrangement with Japan's National Police Agency from 9 November to speed up anti-fraud cooperation.
breaking.source_name: TBS NEWS DIG, 5 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
breaking.summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation said on 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to its email-delivery contractor Arara's 'Arara Message' service leaked 227,216 email addresses — the recipients of emails the bank sent between 1 July and 31 October, mainly corporate customers and some sole proprietors. No account numbers, balances, PINs or internet-banking IDs or passwords were included. The bank was told of the unauthorised access on 28 October and received confirmation of the leak on 2 November.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — third-party data breach
breaking.unknown: The cause of the unauthorised access at the contractor and the full extent of any further exposure are still being checked with the contractor. Whether any leaked addresses have been used in phishing has not been reported.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer banks using third-party or supplier-built mobile banking systems should review supplier security settings, account-enumeration controls and verification for non-designated transfers, and check whether any supplier system permits transfers without the customer logging in. APAC banks should watch the regulator's detailed report due 12 November.
breaking.headline: Bank SinoPac confirms hackers exploited supplier flaw in unauthorised transfers
breaking.known: At a press conference on the evening of 4 November, reported by Focus Taiwan (CNA) at 21:01 SGT, the bank said external hackers breached security settings at the supplier of its new online banking transaction system, used trial-and-error to obtain valid accounts sharing an ID-number prefix, and moved funds to a single Taipei Fubon Bank account, which was frozen. The bank said it reimbursed customers on 3 November, found no evidence of personal-data leakage, hired an independent cybersecurity team, shared threat information with peers via F-ISAC, and will seek compensation from the foreign supplier, whose system is used by no other bank in Taiwan. Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission requires a detailed major-incident report by 12 November.
breaking.summary: Taiwan's Bank SinoPac said on 4 November 2026 that external hackers exploited security settings at the supplier of its new mobile banking system, causing 427 unauthorised transfers totalling about NT$41.76 million (about US$1.27 million) on 3 November. The bank has reimbursed affected customers, the single receiving account at another bank was frozen, and the new system has been suspended.
breaking.unknown: The supplier's name, the exact flaw in its security settings, and the attackers' identity are undisclosed, and the case is under criminal investigation. Local reports of the bank's press conference put the affected customer count at 418, against the Financial Supervisory Commission / Focus Taiwan figure of 419 accounts for the same 427 transfers; the wire uses the regulator's figure and flags the one-customer discrepancy.

breaking.bfsi_impact: A named European bank victim with fraudulent transactions: peer banks should review controls on large and exchange-account withdrawals, verify transaction authorisation and suspension procedures, and watch for laundering of any linked funds through exchanges and instant-swap services. Under the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act, major ICT incidents carry a short initial reporting window, so EU-regulated peers should check their own incident-classification clocks. Third-party platform access is now a confirmed route in this case: review service-provider platforms that can reach the bank directly, not only customer-facing channels.
breaking.headline: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms cyberattack enabling fraudulent transactions
breaking.known: The bank's own statement, reported by CoinDesk, Bloomberg and Ledger Insights on 4 November, confirms the attack and the fraudulent transactions. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT first flagged a suspected loss of more than $106 million at an unnamed EU entity on 2 November and named Arkéa on 3 November, putting the total above $133 million; Bitquery traced $108.8 million in USDC withdrawals from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX accounts over 1–2 November, and Crypto.com said it blocked funds linked to the incident. In a further statement on the evening of 4 November, reported by AFP/Reuters and updated by CNA at 00:57 SGT on 5 November, the bank said attackers reached Arkéa directly through the platform of one of its service providers — not through Fortuneo, and not through client accounts — used the bank's own account to transfer funds to other banks, and then converted funds into cryptocurrency via specialist platforms; a portion of funds was blocked and recovery efforts are under way. The bank gave a provisional estimate of about €100 million, validated the order of magnitude of the reported $133 million (about €118 million) figure, but has not confirmed a final figure. The Paris public prosecutor's office has opened an investigation into an attack on an automated data processing system by an organised group. On 5 November the bank said nearly all operations had resumed after security checks and additional safeguards, customer funds were unaffected, and the losses were lower than the $133 million figure reported in the press and not of a nature to undermine the group's financial strength. On 6 November the president of the Crédit Mutuel confederation, Daniel Baal, told France 5 television that the bank had “already recovered part of (the missing money) today”, without saying how much; Le Télégramme put the amount taken at €118 million.
breaking.source_name: Reuters / AFP via CNA, 4-5 November 2026; Cointelegraph, 5 November 2026
breaking.summary: French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed on 4 November 2026 that it was the target of a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions. The bank says the incident is now under control, some transactions were temporarily suspended, regulators and supervisory authorities have been notified, and clients face no financial consequences. In its evening update the bank gave a provisional estimate of about €100 million, with the final figure still being assessed.
breaking.unknown: The bank has not confirmed a final amount, the attack method, which service provider's platform was used, whether the provider itself was breached (reported by Le Figaro, not confirmed by the bank), or how much, if anything, has been recovered. The $133 million figure is the investigator's estimate, repeated in the press, not a bank-confirmed loss; the bank has validated only its order of magnitude.

entries.bfsi_impact: Chainalysis KYT and address screening are used by banks, exchanges and payment firms for crypto transaction monitoring and sanctions screening. With KYT and the login portal offline and all users required to reset passwords and rotate API keys, firms relying on Chainalysis screening face disrupted transaction monitoring and should treat any Chainalysis-branded password-reset or support message as suspect, since exposed names, roles and live tokens enable convincing impersonation of compliance staff and customers. No investigative graph data or attribution data is reported accessed, so the direct risk is credential and session abuse, not corrupted blockchain attribution.
entries.headline: Chainalysis says breach exposed credentials and live tokens for all customers; KYT screening taken offline
entries.known: Chainalysis first disclosed on 30 October that an attacker using what it called 'offensive agentic techniques' accessed customer names, email addresses, user IDs and organisation role labels, initially described as non-sensitive identity metadata. In updates on 4 November the company said an 'on-path' (man-in-the-middle) attack had exposed a subset of customer passwords and it locked affected accounts. In a further update at 23:00 ET on 4 November it said it had discovered on Monday 2 November that names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed to a malicious actor. The company took its login portal offline, together with Reactor, Data Solutions, the Know-Your-Transaction (KYT) user interface and API, and address-screening products, after detecting further abnormal activity, and asked customers to supply trusted IP addresses for an allowlist before resetting passwords and rotating API keys. On 6 November it began restoring KYT and address screening in phases; Reactor and Data Solutions remained offline. The company says it has no evidence investigative graph data was accessed or attribution data manipulated, and that the incident is unrelated to the Binance theft.
entries.summary: Blockchain-intelligence firm Chainalysis widened its account of its late-October breach: names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all customers were exposed, and its KYT transaction-screening service and login portal were taken offline. Financial institutions using Chainalysis for crypto screening face disrupted monitoring and a phishing and impersonation risk from the exposed credentials.
entries.type: Supplier breach — crypto compliance and screening vendor
entries.unknown: How the attacker got in, which internal tools were reached, how long they had access, and how many organisations are affected have not been disclosed. The attacker is not identified. It is not yet clear how many KYT accounts were accessed without authorisation; Chainalysis says it is directly notifying affected customers.

entries.bfsi_impact: Regulator outreach signals official concern that crypto-market incidents can ripple into traditional finance. Banks should expect follow-up questions on crypto-adjacent exposures and be ready to evidence their own checks after the Binance hack.
entries.headline: US regulators contact banks to check systems after $6.34bn Binance hack
entries.known: Reuters reported that supervisors from the US Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency began contacting banks on Monday morning to ask whether they had detected unusual activity or service disruptions after the $6.34 billion Binance hack of 29 October. A US bank official who received the inquiry said the institution had experienced no significant service disruptions. US banks are conducting their own system reviews, and one of the largest US banks contacted Binance's security personnel directly within hours of the hack. South Korea's Financial Services Commission held an emergency meeting on Monday with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Korea Financial Security Institute, the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance and major virtual-asset service providers to review access controls, wallet withdrawal approval and signing procedures, and administrator privilege management.
entries.source_name: Korea Herald Business, 6 November 2026, citing Reuters
entries.summary: US financial regulators have begun contacting banks to check for unusual activity or service disruptions after the $6.34 billion Binance hack of 29 October; no bank has reported a disruption. South Korea's Financial Services Commission held an emergency meeting with crypto exchanges on Monday to review security controls.
entries.unknown: Which banks were contacted and what, if anything, was found have not been reported. No bank has reported a disruption linked to the Binance hack.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, a US private bank's customer and signer records held by its analytics vendor are exposed. Peer banks should check what client data sits with analytics and AI vendors, review vendor access and exfiltration controls, and watch for phishing or impersonation using signer and account details. Until verified, treat this as an unconfirmed claim, not a confirmed breach.
entries.headline: N0n ransomware group claims Scry Analytics leak exposed US private-banking client records
entries.known: The N0n extortion group listed Scry Analytics, a US data-analytics and AI services firm, on its leak site; the listing was discovered on 6 November at 01:22 UTC (09:22 SGT). The post claims the exposed material includes core banking customer and signer records of a US private banking client — names, account records, signer roles, addresses and contact details — plus a global insurance group's party master of 7,904 legal-entity records with relationship structures, and production support-call transcripts and recordings containing consumer names and mobile numbers. The post says the data was held under contract and marks it 'not paid — exposed'. No ransom amount is stated and no encryption is claimed.
entries.source_name: ransomware.live / RedPacket Security, 6 November 2026 (leak-site listing, unconfirmed)
entries.summary: The N0n extortion group claims a leak from US analytics firm Scry Analytics exposed core customer and signer records of a US private banking client, plus an insurance group's party master of 7,904 records and support-call recordings. The claim rests on the group's own leak-site post only — neither Scry Analytics nor the bank has confirmed it — so it is carried here as reported / unconfirmed.
entries.type: Unverified leak-site claim — third-party data exposure
entries.unknown: The private banking client is not named. There is no confirmation from Scry Analytics or the bank, and no independent verification that the data was exfiltrated or is genuine. The compromise date and method are not stated — the post date is not the compromise date.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks, payment aggregators and fintech partners with Indian operations or Indian payment-API exposure should check API inventories, shut down dormant or test interfaces, enforce beneficiary verification and cooling periods, and flag ₹1-scale test transfers to new beneficiaries followed by larger transfers. ARTEX is already tracked in the Storm-0940/ARTEX deep-research page.
entries.headline: CERT-In warns India's BFSI sector of escalating AI-driven ‘Crafty Falcon’ payment-API attacks
entries.known: The advisory, issued 4 November and reported widely on 5 November, updates CERT-In's 9 October advisory on payment and disbursement API abuse. CERT-In's CSIRT-Fin says successful attacks continue to be reported, including by NBFCs and fintech firms that had already received earlier restricted advisories and taken remedial measures, and that remediated entities have been deliberately re-targeted after incomplete remediation. Attackers use publicly available AI-driven tools — ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI — to survey targets, generate tailored attack scripts and execute full attack chains at machine speed, invoking victims' own payment and disbursement APIs to move funds to mule accounts, after testing routes with micro-value transactions as small as ₹1. Merchant settlement APIs were abused and cryptocurrency wallet keys stolen. Attacks were timed to coincide with weekends and public holidays. CERT-In advised 24x7 monitoring, API inventories with dormant interfaces shut down, beneficiary-name verification and cooling periods for new beneficiaries.
entries.source_name: Indian Express, 5 November 2026; PTI via Rediff, 4 November 2026
entries.summary: India's CERT-In issued an advisory on 4 November 2026 naming the AI-assisted threat actor CRAFTY FALCON and warning that attacks abusing banks', NBFCs' and fintech firms' own payment and disbursement APIs for unauthorised fund transfers are active, ongoing and escalating.
entries.unknown: No individual victim institution was named in the public reporting of the advisory, and no aggregate loss figure for the current escalation was published. Whether any affected entity is a bank with Singapore or APAC operations beyond India is not stated.

entries.bfsi_impact: APAC banks and firms with Korean operations should watch the FSC inspection programme and the planned CEO-accountability measures; the wave shows small virtual-asset and electronic-payment firms are the weakest link, and leaked personal data may feed voice-phishing against bank customers.
entries.headline: South Korea regulator discloses 40 breaches at 37 financial firms; sector-wide inspections ordered
entries.known: The Financial Services Commission announced the measures on 5 November at an industry-wide forum chaired by Chairman Lee Eok-won, attended by the Financial Supervisory Service and the Korea Financial Security Institute. No individual users have yet suffered direct financial losses, and no account passwords that could enable fraudulent transactions were confirmed among the leaked data. The FSC will inspect about 580 financial entities by year-end, plans to lift network-separation rules, launch an AI-based security framework, and draft a Digital Finance Safety Act by the first quarter of 2027. The incidents include previously reported breaches at brokerages, insurers and virtual-asset firms.
entries.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission said 40 cybersecurity incidents were reported at 37 financial firms between 30 September and 5 November 2026, exposing about 473,000 records, with about ₩1 billion (about US$746,000) stolen from company-managed funds at some electronic financial service providers, virtual asset businesses and P2P lenders.
entries.unknown: The FSC has not named all 37 firms or broken down the 40 incidents by firm, and whether any leaked data is exploited in secondary crime such as voice phishing remains unconfirmed.
